messages:
tess: Heads-up: onboarding marabou12b-int4 is hitting OOMs in canary at ~3k concurrent tokens. stacktrace pasted below. anyone seen this pattern before?
omar: ugh. is this coldstart or steady-state?
tess: Mostly steady-state after a few long sessions. coldstarts are fine. logs show kv cache growth + a few allocation failures.
jia: paste the trace?
tess: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 48.00 GiB total capacity; 43.3 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 42.80 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  File "serve/runtime/queue.py", line 214, in process_request
    allocate_kv_slot(request)
  File "serve/kv/cache.py", line 88, in allocate_kv_slot
    buf = torch.empty(sz, dtype=torch.uint8, device='cuda')
```

omar: looks like fragmentation + big max_new_tokens on a few requests. which default max_new_tokens are we using for marabou?
tess: 2048 default in model-config. some clients send 1500 prompts + 1200 max_new_tokens - total sequences are spiking.
kai: we should lower the per-model default to 512 for now and enforce per-route caps. also enable KV trim-on-evict for this model.
jia: agreed. quick mitigation: set model-config: {"max_new_tokens_default": "512", "batch_size": "8", "kv_eviction_policy": "aggressive"} and soft-reserve 8% GPU memory.
omar: soft-reserve helped on phoenix last month. how do we set soft-reserve for Dedicated pools? infra-bot: Deploy plan created: deploy/patches/marabou12b-softreserve-1716754321 -> staging. (CI run 1/3 passed) :robot_face:
tess: test plan: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 512 2) microbatching window 50ms 3) batch_size cap 8 4) enable kv-trim threshold = 0.6 5) soft-reserve 8% 6) enable slot-compactor every 30m
kai: also add a cheap guard in runtime: if request.tokens_pending + request.max_new_tokens > 2500 -> reject with 413 and hint. saves us from these huge combos.
jia: +1 on runtime guard. we had similar at lucent13b. i'll whip a patch.
omar: do we need quantization revert? marabou int4 quality is OK in evals but maybe int4 kernel fragmentation is worse.
tess: evals show low quality delta vs int8, so reverting would increase cost significantly. prefer runtime + config mitigations first.
kai: can we pre-allocate small KV slab on load to reduce fragmentation? like pre-warm 1GiB then release to free list.
jia: there is a prewarm path but it was disabled because of memory pressure on small GPUs. we can make it conditional for 48GB nodes only.
tess: action items: 1) jia -> runtime guard + hotfix PR (ETA 3h) 2) kai -> model-config patch (max_new_tokens 512, batch_size 8, kv_policy aggressive) -> roll to staging (ETA 1h) 3) omar -> run defrag job on canary nodes (slot-compactor) and monitor (ETA 30m) 4) tess -> update eval dashboards and add prompts that spike tokens for regression tests.
ajia: quick command to repro locally if folks want to try: 
```
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' \
  -d '{"model":"marabou12b-int4","prompt":"<long chat>...","max_new_tokens":1200,"batch_size":16}'
```

omar: I'll run a runbook: reduce max_new_tokens for existing sessions? risky. maybe only reject new requests above cap.
kai: canary rollout strategy: 10% traffic with new config + guard, drop to 0 on 5% OOMs per host.
tess: logging note: emit kv_cache.size and kv_frag_ratio metrics at 10s resolution for this model so we can see fragmentation growth.
infra-bot: Metric alert created: marabou12b.kv_frag_ratio > 0.7 for 2m -> page oncall.
jia: deployed runtime guard PR -> #12345. staging smoke green.
kai: model-config patch applied to staging. infra-bot: Patch rollout: staging -> canary (10%) done. (monitoring window open for 20m)
omar: after 15m canary, hosts A and B showed spikes but no OOMs, frag_ratio peaked 0.68 then drifted down after slot-compactor run.
tess: good signs. let's hold at 10% for 2h, then increase to 50% if stable.
jia: PR to reject oversized requests returns JSON: {"error":"max_total_tokens_exceeded","hint":"reduce max_new_tokens or chunk prompt"} (will add link to docs).
kai: don't forget to update default in model catalog UI so new users don't hit this.
tess: will do. thanks team! :thumbsup:
omar: thumbs. if anything else pops up ping #eng-ml.
infra-bot: Canaries stable at 10% for 40m. No OOM pages.
tess: moving to postmortem-ish note: add a perf-eval case that runs mixed-length sessions to catch this earlier next time.
